title: Choose the visual world
question: Three-pane layout is locked. Now the look: keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Soft depth
options.lineage: a warm charcoal studio desk at night
options.thesis: Warm charcoal surfaces stacked by depth, cards tinted by their label, one ember color only for what the keyboard is on.
options.viewport: Translucent board sidebar, four charcoal lanes of label-tinted cards, the selected card lifted in ember, its notes open in the inspector.
options.risk: Dark and soft can turn muddy if the surface steps are too close; contrast must be measured, not guessed.

raised.raise: Ember is reserved for the selected card and keyboard focus. Nothing else on screen uses it.
Focus is the organizing state: the selected card lifts one surface step and shows its first notes line.
Nothing labeled twice: counts are bare numerals, inspector fields carry no labels their content already says.
The ground is never flat: the charcoal drifts warmer toward the lower right.
Every card keeps one size grammar in every lane; Done changes one thing only.

options.label: Keycap
options.lineage: doubleshot keycap colorways from the custom keyboard scene
options.thesis: The board wears a warm putty keycap colorway, and every shortcut shows as a sculpted key that presses down when you hit it.
materials: sculpted keys with a dished top
options.viewport: Cream lanes on a putty desk, grey mod-key sidebar, key hints as real keycaps beside every action, the red key marking the selection.
options.risk: The most familiar look in the builder scene; keycaps must stay hints, never become the cards themselves.

options.label: Specimen
options.thesis: Paper white and ink black, letterforms carry everything, and one density axis remaps the whole board live.
materials: ink type at large scale contrast
options.viewport: Huge column counts set in the type, cards as pure type on paper steps, a density readout in the toolbar that reflows every lane.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: Cmd plus and minus morph the board from dense to roomy, a real win at half-screen width. Loses narrowly on warmth.
options.risk: Pure type and paper can read as a document, not an app, if the lanes lose their surface steps.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark grey project tool look with a violet accent, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: The board the category always ships.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other board app.
